events.title: Khuc Thua Du establishes autonomy
events.description: Taking advantage of the Tang dynasty's decline, Khuc Thua Du (from Cuc Bo Village) raised troops, captured Tong Binh Prefecture (Hanoi), and declared himself Military Governor, ending more than 1,000 years of Northern domination and laying the foundation for the nation's independence.

events.title: Van Kiep Victory
events.description: Hung Dao Vuong Tran Quoc Tuan chose Van Kiep as his headquarters and key defense area. Here, the army and people of the Tran Dynasty organized many fierce intercepting battles, contributing significantly to the victory of the second resistance war against the Mongol-Yuan invaders.

events.title: The fall of Hai Duong Citadel
events.description: French troops mobilized warships and infantry to attack Hai Duong Citadel. Although the royal court's troops fought back, due to the disparity in firepower, the citadel fell to the French, marking the establishment of colonial rule in this land.

events.title: Establishment of the first Party Cell
events.description: In Mao Dien Hamlet, the first Communist Party Cell of Hai Duong Province was established with 3 members. This was a milestone marking the beginning of a tightly organized revolutionary movement in the locality.

events.title: Uprising to seize power in the provincial capital
events.description: Tens of thousands of people from districts flocked to Hai Duong Town, organizing a large rally at the People's Theater (Con Co Cinema), then occupying public offices and seizing power 2 days earlier than Hanoi.

events.title: "Thunder on Route 5" movement
events.description: The army and people of Hai Duong (especially in Kim Thanh and Cam Giang) launched guerrilla warfare along National Route 5 and the Hanoi - Hai Phong railway line. Mine attacks and train derailments turned this vital route into a "deadly road" for French troops.

events.title: Groundbreaking of the Bac - Hung - Hai Great Irrigation Project
events.description: Prime Minister Pham Van Dong struck the first hoe to start construction of the Bac Hung Hai irrigation project at Xuan Quan sluice gate. This was the largest irrigation system in the North at that time, solving the irrigation and drainage issues for the three provinces of Bac Ninh, Hung Yen, and Hai Duong.

events.title: Battle to protect Phu Luong Bridge
events.description: The US Air Force began fiercely bombing Phu Luong Bridge and Lai Vu Bridge to cut off the strategic transport route to Hai Phong Port. Hai Duong's air defense forces and self-defense militia fought resiliently, shooting down many US aircraft to protect the bridges.

events.title: Establishment of Hai Hung Province
events.description: Merging the two provinces of Hai Duong and Hung Yen into Hai Hung Province according to the Resolution of the National Assembly Standing Committee, aiming to concentrate human and material resources for the resistance war against the US to save the country.

events.title: Re-establishment of Hai Duong Province
events.description: The 9th National Assembly passed a Resolution to split Hai Hung Province back into the two provinces of Hai Duong and Hung Yen. Hai Duong Province officially operated under the new administrative unit from January 1, 1997.
